items.title: Beyond tree cover: mapping the world’s forest types
items.summary: A global map categorizing every 10-meter patch of land on Earth into distinct forest types.
items.content:
Maxim Neumann and Charlotte Stanton

A new 10-meter resolution map shows which of the world's forests are natural, planted, or farmed, and how they are changing over time

Protecting the planet's forests starts with a simple question: what type of forest are we looking at? From space, an old-growth rainforest, a eucalyptus plantation, and an oil palm estate can look like the same patch of green. But they hold very different amounts of carbon and biodiversity. Telling them apart, and knowing how each patch has changed over time, shows us where conservation is working and where natural forests are being converted into plantations and farms.

Today, Google DeepMind and Google Research, together with the World Resources Institute (WRI) and the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA), are releasing Forest Typology (ForTy) 2020 , a global map that categorizes every 10-by-10-meter patch of land on Earth into six distinct forest and land-use types, a key baseline for the EU's deforestation regulation. Alongside it, we're sharing an early time series that tracks how these forests changed each year from 2017 to 2025, including where natural forests were replaced by plantations or farms. For the first time, users can see at 10-meter detail worldwide, year by year, not just where forest was lost, but what replaced it: a timber plantation, a tree-crop farm or other land.

All forests store carbon and, together, forests are home to most of the world's land-based plant and animal species. But a forest’s ecological value also depends on its history: a primary forest that has never been cleared holds far more carbon and biodiversity than a single-species timber plantation that is harvested every decade or two.

Most global maps only indicate whether trees are present. That's a challenge for those trying to protect natural forests. The European Union's regulation on deforestation-free products (EUDR), for example, requires that products like coffee, cocoa or palm oil do not originate from land that was forest in 2020 and has since been converted to agriculture. Similarly, wood products, such as furniture, must also be free of forest degradation: they can't come from primary forests that have since been converted into plantation or planted forests, or from naturally regenerating forests that have since been converted into plantation forests. As a result, companies and regulators need to know not just where trees are, but what kind of forest they form (primary or regrowing, planted or plantation, forest or farm) and what replaces that forest after a harvest.

Last year, we jointly released Natural Forests of the World 2020 , a 10-meter resolution global map that separated natural forests from all other tree cover. It offered a starting point to help companies and regulators implement the EU Deforestation Regulation, and to support commodity producers in meeting their commitments not to convert natural forest. That map answered one question for every patch of land: was it natural forest in 2020 or not? ForTy goes further, showing what kind of forest is there, from primary forest to timber plantation to tree crops, and, with the new time series, how that changes each year.

Specifically, ForTy sorts land into six categories based on definitions from the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO):

The Forest Typology map for 2020. Each color shows the most common forest or land type in each square kilometer. Explore it at 10-meter detail in our Earth Engine app .

Training our ForTy model was challenging because these categories depend in part on how land is used, not just how it looks. To teach our model the difference, we built a large-scale collection of forest-type examples with about 1.7 million labeled locations drawn from expert surveys, national and regional datasets, and targeted reviews of places where the model struggled. The model uses a custom architecture designed for the challenges of remote sensing data, and takes as a key input AlphaEarth Foundations embeddings , data-compact summaries of years of satellite observations for each 10-meter pixel, so it can spot subtle clues like planting patterns, growth cycles and harvest rhythms.

From above, the five forest and tree-crop classes can look alike. ForTy is able to identify the subtle differences in structure and seasonal patterns that set them apart, accurately categorizing them in a global map database. Imagery © Google Earth, Maxar Technologies, Airbus.

A map is only useful if people can trust it. So, with IIASA and WRI, we validated ForTy against more than 9,000 randomly chosen sites around the world. At each site, two trained experts studied high-resolution imagery and years of satellite records to determine which type of land was really there. ForTy picked the right forest type 90% of the time, and told forest apart from non-forest land 95% of the time, outperforming other global forest maps.

Beyond accuracy, we know that global conservation is not one-size-fits-all. Instead of giving a yes-or-no label for a specific patch of land, ForTy provides a probability score for each class, enabling users to adapt the classification to regional contexts and application-specific precision trade-offs. For example, a company assessing deforestation risk under EUDR might set a strict threshold, only accepting pixels the model is highly certain about to avoid regulatory risks. Meanwhile, a researcher estimating total forest extent might use the full spectrum of probabilities to get a fuller picture of the potential landscape.

A map of a single year is a useful baseline, but forests change. Our new early-release time series applies a similar approach to every year from 2017 to 2025. It shows not only where forests disappear and where they grow back, but also what kind of change happened: a natural forest turned into a timber plantation, for example, or abandoned land slowly regenerating into forest.

items.content:
The Cool X Wide’s screen has a 16:10 aspect ratio but doesn’t come with the cost or challenges of a folding display.

The design of widescreen folding phones like the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 , Huawei Pura X View , and now the iPhone Duo , is starting to influence traditional slab phones. Similar to the Huawei Pura X View that launched in China in August, the new Coolpad Cool X Wide has a much wider screen than what’s typically seen in non-folding phones. The screen real estate is more on par with what you get from a tiny tablet , or what the iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8 offer when closed, minus huge price tags , budget-stressing repair costs , and inevitable screen creases .

The Cool X Wide’s 6.38-inch display has a 16:10 aspect ratio with refresh rates up to 90Hz and a 1,158x720 resolution. There’s also a 50-megapixel main camera on the back and a 4,600mAh battery. It comes with Android 16 out of the box, but the phone’s processor limits its connectivity to only 4G networks, as Android Authority points out.

If you’re wondering how a device with a 16:10 screen will feel in hand, the Cool X Wide is nearly exactly as tall as the iPhone 18 Pro, but while Apple’s latest is 2.83 inches wide, the new Coolpad is 3.72 inches.

items.title: Developer platform Railway urges ‘all users’ to revoke secret keys after cyberattack
items.summary: The vibe-coding platform said all of its customers should revoke and rotate their private keys, after hackers were able to decrypt some customer secrets.
items.content:
Development platform Railway has confirmed that a cyberattack allowed hackers to access some customer secrets, prompting the company to urge all users to rotate their API and cloud keys amid fears of a broader breach of customer data.

The company, which allows customers to build apps and services on its cloud development platform, said in a blog post on Wednesday that the unidentified hackers “may have accessed encrypted environment variables and, for some of them, obtained the decrypted contents.”

These environment variables are typically lists of passwords and API keys that are used by the developer’s apps to access other services, such as cloud data storage and databases. With these customer secrets, an attacker could also log in and access data as if they were the rightful owner.

Railway said that while its initial analysis suggests the breach was limited to a “subset of users,” it suggested that “all users” should revoke and rotate all of their keys so that attackers cannot abuse them.

The company also said it paused customer deployments while the company investigates, effectively freezing customer websites and apps.

Railway did not say how many specific users were affected, or what was the root cause of the incident. The company did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the incident, or whether it has received any correspondence from the hackers, such as a ransom demand.

It’s unclear how the attack went down or which Railway systems were compromised. Railway said that the breach was likely part of a broader attack targeting platforms “with the aim of compromising AI inference providers.” These kinds of attacks involve tricking AI systems into leaking sensitive data through malicious prompts beyond their guardrails.

The latest breach comes soon after U.S. cybersecurity agency CISA warned that China-based AI companies are conducting large-scale attacks on U.S. companies with the aim of improving their own models.

Earlier this week, open source AI coding tool OpenCode said customer secrets had been breached in a similar attack, with hackers taking more than 1% of its customers’ API keys and other secrets. OpenCode attributed the attack to an AI distillation attack, where large numbers of agents seek to extract sensitive information from AI models.

The Railway attack appears to be separate from two critical security vulnerabilities publicly disclosed in the PHP web programming language this week , prompting companies and governments around the world to pull down their sites to fix the vulnerability before attackers could exploit it. (PHP is used in some 70% of websites and public-facing internet systems.)

Patches for the bug, dubbed “PHP2Shell,” were publicly released on Wednesday , following a global coordinated effort to allow big organizations to fix their systems ahead of possible attacks. Security researchers at Amazon said they found evidence of exploitation four days before the patch releases, suggesting that the bugs are now being used in attacks.

items.title: Bill Gates says to prepare for 20 years of ‘tumultuous’ AI disruption
items.summary: Today, I’m talking to Bill Gates, cofounder and former CEO of Microsoft and chairman of the Gates Foundation. You may have noticed Bill in the news more lately — he’s been on something of a tour for the past few months, ever since publishing an essay in late August titled “The tu
items.content:
The Microsoft cofounder isn’t an AI doomer, but he says it’s still “the most dangerous weapon of all time.”

Today, I’m talking to Bill Gates, cofounder and former CEO of Microsoft and chairman of the Gates Foundation.

You may have noticed Bill in the news more lately — he’s been on something of a tour for the past few months, ever since publishing an essay in late August titled “The turbulent AI era is here. The choices we make now are critical.”

In his piece, Gates ratcheted up his rhetoric around AI safety, writing that “even under the best circumstances, the transition to this new AI era will be one of the most turbulent times in human history.”

In interviews since , Gates has called AI “the most dangerous thing that humans have ever gone near,” and that AI “makes nuclear weapons look like nothing.” It is clear he does not think the current policy response from the White House, or the lack of coordinated efforts from the AI industry itself, is sufficient to combat this threat.

So I wanted to know: Is Bill Gates an AI doomer? I also had a series of questions downstream from what he’s been arguing about AI. How can we ever hope to control AI, and align it to humanity, if we can’t even agree on what it is and whether it’s conscious ? How would you even technically construct a solution to alignment that could be enforced, not just for closed-source models but open-source ones, too?

Bill gave us a big chunk of his time to dig into these issues with him, and the resulting conversation is a really illuminating one. He thinks we need to prepare for roughly two decades of AI disruption, and he says this period could be so painful it might split society in two — between people comfortable living near the technological frontier, and those who reject it.

We also talked about the labor considerations, the nihilism of younger generations toward technological progress, and what should make us hopeful about the future. This is a deep one.

Okay: Bill Gates, the cofounder and former CEO of Microsoft. Here we go.

This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity.

Bill Gates, you are the co-founder and former CEO of Microsoft. You’re also the chairman of the Gates Foundation. Welcome to Decoder .

It’s good to talk to you again. You and I have spoken many times over the years. I would say that the circumstances of this conversation feel very different. Previously, when you and I would talk, you were always very hopeful about technology and what it could bring.

You had a Netflix series a few years ago. You talked to The Verge , and I want to just read you this quote. You said, “I believe AI is a beneficial thing, we just need to shape it in the right way.” I would say you still agree with that, you just think the time to shape it is now.

Yeah, I agree with that. I’d say the response broadly hasn’t been adequate to the speed that the challenge is arising. I’m very concerned that the bad stuff will not be minimized and that a lot of good stuff could come fairly slowly if we don’t manage it the right way.

I’m very concerned that the bad stuff will not be minimized and that a lot of good stuff could come fairly slowly if we don’t manage it the right way

I want to have this conversation with you in three parts. I want to understand how you feel about AI as a technology today and why it’s advancing so quickly. I’m very curious about the technology, and the technical solutions to potentially control it. There are policy solutions as well, but it seems like we have to build an awful lot of technology.

I’m also very curious to talk about who might impose those solutions and controls, because that seems very much up for debate right now as well. So let’s just start at the start. What has made you feel the urgency that AI is arriving at a speed that means we’re not ready to control it?

The progress over the last year has been really quite amazing, starting with the ability to write code and find cyber flaws, the ability to reason in biology, the ability to form relationships with kids or other people, the ability to disrupt the job market. The incredible power that exists today means that every one of those things will happen and society needs to be ready.

Do you see that happening as a technology as a whole or in the products that are instantiated by the companies that are making AI today?

What I mean is that AI is a broad set of models that exist in the world, some open source, some proprietary. Then there are the companies that make these products and there are the leaders of those companies that make these products.

At every level, there’s a different relationship you or I might have to AI. Are you seeing these risks and these capabilities broadly in the field, or in the particular companies led by the particular people?

The risk isn’t one model versus another model. Certainly, the near-term danger of models where you can remove all the safeguards is very high and quite different from models where you monitor to make sure that cyberattackers and bioterrorists are not able to exploit the capability of the model to do gigantic harm.

The big near-term risk really comes from models without safeguards. On a longer timeframe, the control issue relates to any state-of-the-art model, but it’s always easier when you can make sure safeguards are maintained.

The reason I’m asking that question that way is maybe you don’t trust Sam Altman today, but you trust Dario Amodei. Or maybe you don’t trust either one of those and you trust Satya Nadella at Microsoft, and that is a market dynamic where maybe we’re all going to pick the safest model or the safest company, and you think that is diffuse.

You think eventually the technology will just get to a place where it’s harmful or can cause these harms because it exists?

For somebody doing a cyberattack with the model, it’s not about choosing a model. It doesn’t matter what model you choose.

items.title: Claude Duet app is Anthropic’s bet on agents
items.summary: Claude Duet is available through waitlist for Pro and Max plan users
items.content:
The AI world is flooded with personal and productivity-based assistants , with new ones launching every week. Now, Anthropic is entering this battle in the hopes of gaining user attention with a new app called Claude Duet, aimed at rivaling Meta Muse , OpenAI Dots , Hark , Instinct , Grok Bot , and Fo .

Anthropic said the new agent is meant to cater to professionals and small businesses to help them with automating and managing tasks. The company is making a distinction from personal agents such as Instinct , by noting that Duet isn’t good at handling errands or booking tickets, and it can’t show you its browser use as it happens.

Instead, Duet can build a daily briefing for its users, create dashboards, or suggest actions based on the user’s data. Like other agents, Duet can complete tasks in the background through its own virtual machine while you handle other things, then come back to you if it needs your approval.

The launch arrives as the market shifts beyond AI assistants to agents that can work on users’ behalf. Many of Anthropic’s rivals are focusing on business use cases. While Meta’s Muse is a personal AI assistant, the company also released a version to cater to small businesses with connections to other apps . OpenAI’s Dots has a business slant as well, with its integration with professional tools .

Anthropic says Duet proactively delivers its recommendations as it monitors ongoing tasks. Built on the Claude Opus 5.5 model, Duet can connect to over 6,000 connectors and plugins in the Claude Marketplace. It can also make online purchases on users’ behalf via Stripe’s ⁠Link digital wallet or Shopify’s Shop Pay.

The company said sensitive steps like payments would require user approval. However, Duet won’t trade securities or move money between accounts.

Anthropic also released a new classifier to check each message to prevent sensitive information from leaking out. It said that, by default, the agent would turn down requests asking for credit card numbers and government identification.

Claude Duet is available as an app on iOS and Android, and on the web through Claude.ai for Pro and Max customers in research preview. Users have to join a waitlist to try it.

items.title: Nirva raises $33M for a pendant that only listens to you
items.summary: Nirva will ship its $249 ambient AI pendant by the end of the year.
items.content:
Ambient AI is having a moment. Amazon launched a new wrist-worn device with Bee; a former Plaud exec launched ambient apps through a startup called Ambi, which aims to also build its own hardware; and Apple launched Voice Intelligence features during its iPhone launch in September. Now, a company called Nirva is betting on a jewelry-like pendant and its ability to listen only to the wearer.

The startup today announced a new $25 million pre-Series A round, adding to the $8 million it raised earlier in the year from investors like Lightspeed and South Park Commons, bringing its total raise to $33 million.

Nirva was founded in 2025 by two former Meta Reality Labs employees, Wei Lyu and Jason Chen, along with Hanying Hu, who founded a fashion and jewelry brand.

The company’s first device is a pendant, which can also be worn as a bracelet. The device weighs only around eight grams, making it easy to wear all day. Its battery lasts up to three days on a single charge.

Longer term, Nirva aims to release more devices.

In a call with TechCrunch, Nirva CEO Lyu said that the company wanted to build a wearable that blends in with fashion, but also provides value to users.

“This is a piece of jewelry that only focuses on listening to your own speech. We are not like a voice recorder or like a meeting note taker. One key difference between us, Taya, Vocci, or Sandbar Ring is that we’re always passively listening to your own speech. So it’s always on. It keeps modeling the user and modeling your mind,” Lyu said.

For ambient devices, privacy is a big question, as people might not like to be recorded all the time. Plus, devices like the Ray-Ban Meta have instilled fear in those who are around the person wearing the smart glasses that they are being recorded too.

Nirva gets around this problem by asking users to record snippets of their voice during onboarding and building its model based on that. During use, the device filters out conversations or data captured from the other people around the device. That means it’s only recording the wearer.

In addition, Nirva by default doesn’t keep any audio data or transcripts after processing the conversations.

Nirva is positioning itself as a personal insights company rather than a productivity startup. However, its app shows you reminders or action items and ways to act on them. Lyu said that through its app, the startup wants to help users show up for others in a better way in their lives.

“I think there’s no universal way to help everyone to solve their problems. We are building a tool to help people to improve their self-understanding, self-compassion, and self-awareness,” Lyu said.

The companion app parses users’ speech and creates insights that it infers are related to the user’s personality, including patterns, the people who tend to be around them, the places they’ve been to, and other daily notes. Lyu emphasized that the app shows users insights around their emotions, communication style, and ways they can improve.

Wyu gave an example of an incident when she forgot to thank her mother for something, and the app later nudged her with a reminder about this.

The company also said that, before it discards the audio, it’s able to track the tone, pitch, volume, and speed, which are useful for deriving emotion-related understandings that are then surfaced in the app.

Nirva will start taking orders for its devices in November, with an aim to ship them to early users by the end of the year. The $249 device will be available in silver, brushed silver, black, and gold.

The startup has competition in the AI wearables area. There are companies like former Apple employees’ Taya , which is also building intelligent jewelry. Plus, startups like Friend and Bee are trying to be companion gadgets as well.

items.title: Apple will label apps that are ‘Made for iPhone Duo’
items.summary: Apple is rolling out a new badge in the App Store to indicate whether an app is optimized for its new foldable. The new "Made for iPhone Duo" badge will appear across apps and games that work with the device's extra screen real estate. Though Apple doesn't include an image of wha
items.content:
Many apps, including Netflix, Microsoft Word, and Zoom, are taking advantage of the Duo’s extra screen real estate.

Apple is rolling out a new badge in the App Store to indicate whether an app is optimized for its new foldable. The new “Made for iPhone Duo” badge will appear across apps and games that work with the device’s extra screen real estate.

Though Apple doesn’t include an image of what this badge might look like, it highlighted some of the ways apps are taking advantage of the Duo’s inner and outer screens. Netflix, for example, will display shows and movies that take up the whole inner display, while allowing you to watch its feed of short-form clips on the outside. Amazon’s Prime Video will let you watch shows and movies with the Duo partially folded, with the content on top and details about the cast on the bottom.

Meanwhile, Apple says Microsoft Word and Outlook will offer a “desktop-class” experience on the Duo, with Word placing its formatting tools alongside a document, and Outlook displaying your inbox next to a full email. Zoom can also display a video conference alongside shared content across the iPhone Duo’s inner screen. Other apps optimized for the Duo include Paramount Plus, NYT Cooking, Yelp, Lyft, and United Airlines. But, as The Verge ’s Nilay Patel found during his Duo testing , some apps “optimized” for the device, like Instagram, still have some bugs.

Apple says it’s going to launch editorial collections for the iPhone Duo on Friday, “with additional app updates rolling out throughout the year.” The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 and launches on Friday, with “limited” quantities available on a walk-in basis .

items.title: Forget "Malaise 2.0," GM says it's still all-in on EVs and autonomy
items.summary: General Motors' plans will require quite a lot of customers' trust.
items.content:
It’s easy to criticize US automakers and their tepid approach to electric vehicles under the current administration and the expiration of the EV tax credit . It’s also easy to look at the rest of the world’s embrace of EVs and wonder if the US is entering a “Malaise 2.0” era. Which is why GM wants the world to know that it is still focused on its end goals of electrification, autonomy, and improving vehicle quality while reducing development time.

At this year’s GM Forward event, company executives announced that its hands-off, eyes-off Super Cruise technology will expand across the lineup and be available on nearly every vehicle. This will include the pickup trucks and the crossovers, and not just the Escalade IQ that it was announced for last year.

Sterling Anderson, GM’s head of product, said the company is testing this technology to the tune of 1 million miles (1.6 million km) a month in both the virtual and real world. The goal is that not only would the vehicle be able to take you places, but it could go and do things for you.

That sounds rather dystopian. But Anderson told Ars in an interview that once you realize what your vehicle is capable of doing (beyond the paradigm of being a car to go places), it opens up a world of convenience that might be hard to envision right now. He’s not talking about an Optimus-style robot that’ll do your laundry, but a tool that you use every day that expands to do more things.

GM’s newly announced OnStar AI will play a role. “Imagine you worked late, and you get in your car to go home,” he told us. “Your car might remember that you ordered takeout from a restaurant recently that you frequent and like. The car could prompt you and place a pick-up order for you, which will be ready when you arrive to pick it up.”

Trust is the key here, and Anderson reiterated that several times, suggesting that a car might be a more trusted piece of technology than a mobile phone. “People have a relationship with their cars that they don’t have with other things,” he said. “If your phone randomly suggested your favorite restaurant, it might give you pause, but if your car did so within the appropriate context you might be more willing to accept that.”

OnStar AI will do more than just learn your habits; it will be able to help you better understand and better use your vehicle, we’re told. For example: a driver hears the car beep but doesn’t know what the alert was for. In this case, they could ask OnStar and it would be able to tell them—for example, a speed limit warning. Being a specialized AI trained specifically on the details of the car, it can be integrated in a way that other models, like Google’s Gemini, cannot.

Thanks to new compute on board, announced at last year’s Forward , the car will be able to handle much of that processing locally without requiring a connection to the cloud at all. But a cloud connection could improve the drive or make it safer. For some time now, automakers and suppliers have promised systems that crowdsource data to infer and predict road conditions—if you’re driving through a snowy area, and the cars in front of you have had traction control events, you could receive a warning to be extra careful as you approach.

GM also wants to keep customers within its own ecosystem. Imagine a two-car, two-GM OnStar AI household, and you’re late picking up your child from practice. Here, OnStar AI could look and see your spouse is actually closer, swap roles, and re-direct you to the takeout place to pick up dinner. OK, it’s a very specific use case.

Trust continues to be the key. Anderson knows that must be earned, and trust is difficult to get back if it’s broken.

His approach is to put that customer trust first in what he does. For example, GM’s new infotainment system will have the ability to record from the cameras as a dash cam and store that video. And it can upload that video to GM’s cloud to access anywhere. But it is end-to-end encrypted, meaning that when it hits GM’s servers it’s in a format that GM can’t read. If law enforcement wanted to view the video, GM wouldn’t be able to help because it could not decrypt the video.

That is the type of trust that is absolutely needed when dealing with this type of personal data, because there is a convenience to a lot of this. But the opportunity for that data to be misused is also there—it wasn’t too long ago that GM was found to be selling customers’ data , often without their knowledge, to insurance companies.

We’ll want to experience GM’s new attitude in practice, of course, but hearing an automotive executive directly address that concern head-on was refreshing.

This all leads into the fully autonomous functionality that GM is working on. Ars also spoke with Rashed Haq, VP of Autonomous Vehicles at GM, about the current state of the level 4 technology, and more importantly, when it’ll be safe enough for customers to use.

“We look at two key factors, safety and roadcraft,” Haq told me.

Safety obviously includes the vehicle’s occupants, but also the general public. And that requires millions of miles of testing in the real world but also digitally . Automakers like GM will never be able to prepare for every scenario, but it will combine training data with an open vocabulary to assess what information is there and make a driving decision based on that. Haq also reiterated the company’s expectation that when the car is driven by the computer, the responsibility falls on GM and the computer if something goes wrong due to a malfunction.

The second key here is roadcraft. That means making sure that the vehicle isn’t creating a hazard or problem for other vehicles on the road. You’ve likely seen videos where Waymo vehicles are all crowded on a street blocking traffic : That’s not something GM wants its cars to do.

EEvery Googlebook laptop we’ve tested so far has great hardware. The problem is the software. While Googlebook OS has exciting ideas for how a laptop and phone can work together, right now it’s mostly a frustrating experience filled with annoying bugs and lackluster app support . It often feels like using an Android tablet with a keyboard and trackpad grafted on, rather than a cohesive laptop OS. It’s too bad, because those keyboards and trackpads — and pretty much all the laptops’ hardware components — are great.

Frankly, they should be. The cheapest is $900, a price where you start to expect quality processors, metal builds, higher-quality displays, good speakers, and great keyboards and trackpads (even haptic ones in some cases). The Googlebooks have those covered, and they also have very good battery life and at least 16GB of RAM.

Google wanted Googlebooks to feel premium, and HP, Acer, Lenovo, Dell, and Asus all delivered. It’s Google’s software that needs to catch up. In their current state, we don’t recommend you buy any of them. But it’s worth reviewing the hardware to determine which shows the most promise if the software one day improves — or if crafty modders manage to install other operating systems. Since the software is the same on all Googlebooks (save for some preinstalled manufacturer apps), and we’ve already covered that software at length, we’re strictly talking about Googlebook hardware here. The scores, however, cover hardware and software as they stand today. Brace yourself — the scores are bad.

If you’re a dedicated Google user or Pixel fan and you really want to be an early adopter / paying beta tester — or if you’re just here for some schadenfreude — here are our collective thoughts on each and every Googlebook.

The most affordable of the Googlebooks (for now) Nice screen and build

Googlebook OS feels like a beta No portrait orientation in tablet mode

The Acer Googlebook 14 is the only 2-in-1 convertible of the bunch, and it’s one of the nicest-feeling and -looking Acers I’ve ever used at this price. It’s light, with a sturdy metal chassis and a great 2880 x 1800 / 120Hz OLED touchscreen with stylus support. I find 2-in-1s pretty handy, even if they look clunkier than tablets like a Microsoft Surface Pro or an iPad with a keyboard case , but Googlebook OS doesn’t yet support portrait orientation, which limits the Acer’s stylus potential. Like all Googlebooks, the Acer has an Auto-Rotate toggle in settings, but it only flips the orientation 180 degrees — a strange oversight.

The speakers don’t have a lot of bass, and they can get muffled in tablet mode depending on how you hold the laptop, but they’re decent and sound balanced overall. The webcam is a slight weak point, as colors and contrast are a touch drab. But nothing here is bad. This isn’t like some of the Acer Aspires or Swifts I’ve tested in the past where you had to deal with a terrible screen and shoddy build quality for the sake of a good chip. It’s just an all-around nice package. That extends to the battery life, which lasted me eight to nine hours of light-to-mixed usage.

If this was running Windows or a proper Linux distro with the same hardware and price, it’d be a rare bright spot in our ongoing RAMageddon hellscape. But thanks to Googlebook OS, it’s not. And an Acer rep told us its $900 launch price is only available for a limited time. That might sound like an incentive to buy one before a price increase, but please allow me to tap the “Don’t buy it now for what it might do later” sign. Actually, picture me tapping it as you read this whole article.

— Antonio G. Di Benedetto, Laptop Reviewer

Small and light On the cheaper side of Googlebooks Great keyboard and trackpad

Googlebook OS feels like a beta Anti-glare display has some issues Only the two USB-C ports

Here’s my theory: If Googlebooks are going to work anytime soon, they’re going to work as secondary computers. Maybe they don’t need to replace your primary work machine if they can instead be light, fast, simple, and fun to use. (Yes, I agree that $900 or more is a lot to pay for this kind of device, but hey, iPads pull it off!) I already see glimmers of possibility here, even through the bugs of Googlebook OS. “A Chromebook, but also it runs all my apps” is not a bad pitch for an off-day computer.

That’s why, of all the available Googlebooks, the Dell XPS Googlebook makes the most sense to me. At 2.2 pounds, with a 13.4-inch screen, and starting at $999, it’s one of the smallest and lightest Googlebooks available. (And unlike the cheaper Acer Googlebook 14, it doesn’t offer a bunch of flippy tablet modes that don’t really work.) Like the other models we’ve tested, it’s a lovely piece of high-end hardware; I love the keyboard and trackpad, I appreciate that I can open the thing with one hand, and the Qualcomm chip inside does its job fine for all my practical purposes. The battery got me through a full day of travel and then some.

My only real complaint is with the anti-glare coating on the display, which does help tamp down reflections but also creates that slight rainbow-shimmer effect that makes the screen appear a little less sharp and clear. The coating also dims the screen a bit — I’ve used the XPS Googlebook mostly at max brightness, just to get it up to normal. I am generally extremely in favor of these matte displays, but I’d trade the XPS Googlebook’s for a glossy one in a heartbeat.

items.title: 1Password lets AI agents use your passwords without seeing them
items.summary: 1Password is introducing a new feature that allows AI agents to sign into your accounts without actually seeing or handling your passwords. The aptly named 1Password for Agents doesn't give bots free reign to access all of your connected accounts - you'll still need to grant appr
items.content:
Just grant the agent access approval and it’ll sign into your accounts to complete tasks.﻿

1Password is introducing a new feature that allows AI agents to sign into your accounts without actually seeing or handling your passwords. The aptly named 1Password for Agents doesn’t give bots free reign to access all of your connected accounts — you’ll still need to grant approval for sign-in requests — but should make it less cumbersome to use Agents for tasks that require them to log into various services.

”Agents are starting to do real work on our behalf. The old model where you hand over a credential and hope for the best doesn’t work,” 1Password CEO Aashish Tripathi said in a press statement. “An agent should be able to do the job it’s been asked to do without getting permanent access to everything behind the account, and 1Password provides the trust layer that makes this possible across personal agent experiences.”

With this new system, an AI agent uses a unique digital key to verify its identity to 1Password when it reaches a sign-in form. The app then sends you a notification about which account credentials it needs, and why. If you choose to approve the request, 1Password will fill in the required login information instead of handing it to the agent. Approvals are granted on your own device to ensure you’re behind the permissions, making this a similar process to two-factor authentication. After the agent is signed in, it’ll continue with its task, without ever having actually seen your password.

This 1Password access system is designed to work with a variety of popular AI agents, including Meta Muse, ChatGPT Work and Dots, Claude Duet, Grok Bot, and Town. 1Password says more partners are working to bring support to 1Password for Agents, including Browserbase, Browser Use, Dana, Instinct, Kernel, Perplexity, Ramp, Tomo, and Wajo, with “additional integrations to come.”

items.title: Meet Mori, a Cute Robot Mushroom That Doesn’t Really Say (or Do) Anything
items.summary: Step one in convincing people to live with robots with cameras on their faces? Disguise them as cute home decor.
items.content:
You've had a long day. You finally get home, fling the door open, plonk on the couch, and let out a big sigh. In the corner of your eye, you notice your mushroom lamp perk up. Its microphone must have heard you come in. Its head raises to reveal round, animated eyes, and a little diamond-shaped nose—which actually houses a camera.

It does a little jiggle because it sees you're back. Its name is Mori.

As you move around the space—maybe it's time to start cooking dinner—the little robot's face follows you, observing your movements and making soft sounds that are a cross between a bird and R2-D2. The day's stress catches up, and you need a moment to relax, so you head over to Mori, touch its head, and its eyes and camera-nose dip back inside its body. It goes back to being a lamp, except now it plays nature soundscapes so you can feel at ease.

That's the pitch from OKA , or One Kind Artifact, a new startup based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and Shenzhen, China, focusing on experimental technology. CEO Hua Wang tells WIRED he wants his company to create five experimental “Artifacts” over the course of OKA's lifetime. Mori is the first.

“There are certain relationships in this era we want to fix between humans and our surroundings—human with nature, human with one another—every product is an experience trying to reconnect some of those relationships,” Wang says. Before cofounding OKA, he was a general manager at Meipai, a video-sharing app from the Chinese phone brand Meitu. He also cofounded Bondee, a now-defunct social media app that briefly went viral in Asia .

According to the company, the point of Mori, the nearly 12-inch-tall home robot lamp, is to reconnect its owners with nature. It can play nature soundscapes. It will glow different colors—inspired by rain, forests, fire, and wind—while reacting to your movements. It can guide you through a calming breathing session.

It also uses its built-in camera and microphones to serve as a fun little interactive companion in your home. Ask it how your outfit looks, and Mori will jiggle excitedly. If you're playing music or watching TV, Mori can dance to the tunes and react to the action on your TV screen.

It intentionally does not do anything else. Unlike an Amazon Echo , it isn't an assistant: You can't use voice commands to control smart lights or cue up Spotify tracks, and it won't answer if you ask about the weather.

The Founder's Edition is a staggering $649 and is available starting today, though stock is limited to a few hundred units. That price also includes a two-year warranty and two years of Mori's subscription service. If you miss out on the Founder’s Edition, you can still buy a standard edition Mori, but that costs $799, and that higher price shockingly does not include any of the subscription features.

Wang says today's home robots have mostly taken on “machine-like” forms that don't mesh well with personal environments, so OKA designed a lamp that blends in, but is also anthropomorphized to make being at home “feel better.”

It might notice, for example, that you've been on your phone doomscrolling for two hours straight on the couch. Mori might then try to get your attention so you come over, listen to some wind rustling through the leaves, and give your eyes a break. When you're on a phone call, or maybe having an argument with a significant other, it understands what’s happening and goes silent so as not to distract you.

“All gadgets try to capture more of your attention,” Wang says. “Mori gives your attention back to you. It invites you to do meditative experiences. Nature has this restorative power to humans.”

The robot can connect to Wi-Fi, which should give you pause from a security standpoint , but Wang says the internet connection is only used for firmware updates.

Mori processes raw images and audio locally, and then discards the files. Facial feature data—which is collected so it knows to react to you versus a guest—is encrypted on the device, and never uploaded. The camera turns off when the robot retracts into a lamp, and the microphone turns off when you double-tap the top of Mori's head. It is battery-powered, so you can take it from room to room, or just leave it plugged in.

Wang says Mori's skill set is limited for now, though it could expand in the future. He suggests it could connect to your Oura Ring data in the future so it knows exactly when you need some relaxing sounds, or to your Spotify account to play different content. Voice commands could even come later—like asking Mori to play nature sounds instead of having to touch it.

“People feel isolated and want this kind of presence in their home. A lot of people leave their TV on to fill the emptiness of the room,” Wang says, pointing to a time when he was feeling isolated while studying abroad in the US. “It's not particularly for the elderly or children, but for younger generations.”

Cute robot pets that interact with you have been welcomed into our homes before. Chris Harrison, director of the Future Interfaces Group at Carnegie Mellon University, points to Sony's Aibo dog from 1999 as an early digital companion. However, he says the crucial ingredient they have been missing is what artificial intelligence can now provide. These previous robots were too simplistic, but now that the modern versions can understand and react to human actions and emotions, they could become more impactful.

“Humans have always wanted to anthropomorphize everything—they love making things cute,” Harrison says. “We want to make robots cute; we want to put cute little cases on our iPhones.” He points to Meta's new Muse agent , which has a cuddly avatar . “It is almost like a pet, but a hyper-capable pet.”

When I point out that Mori doesn't seem very capable with its limited feature set, Harrison likens it to people owning a goldfish or a hamster.

황고연 대표 "각자 필요한 수준의 정보 얻는 차별화된 뉴스 소비 경험 제공”

모바일 콘텐츠 기업 허블이 이용자의 뉴스 소비 성향에 맞춰 정보의 깊이를 조절하는 AI 뉴스 에이전트 '탭뷰 AI'를 선보인다.

22일 회사에 따르면, 탭뷰 AI는 별도의 앱 설치나 회원가입 절차 없이 기존 제휴 앱 안에서 곧바로 구동되는 인앱 서비스다. 이용자의 개인정보를 수집하지 않고 접속 앱·시간대·지역 정보만으로 소비 성향을 정밀 추정해 맞춤형 뉴스를 제공한다.

특히 화면 스크롤에 따라 정보의 깊이가 단계적으로 심화되는 단일 인터페이스를 갖췄다. 홈 피드의 '유저 맞춤 제목'과 한 줄짜리 '이슈 타임라인'을 필두로, 기사 속 이미지를 모은 '시각 자료 모아보기', 핵심을 세 문장으로 압축한 '3줄 요약', 상황·원인·영향·대응과 입장별 체크포인트를 분석하는 심층 'AI 전문 리포트'까지 5가지 기능을 수직으로 배치했다.

이를 통해 제목만 훑는 독자부터 30초 내 요약을 원하는 독자, 심층 맥락을 파악하려는 독자까지 모드 전환 없이 스크롤만으로 원하는 깊이의 뉴스를 소비할 수 있다.

허블은 기존 모바일 브라우저 광고 플랫폼 '허블뷰'의 SDK가 탑재된 100여개 제휴 앱망을 바탕으로 '탭뷰 AI' SDK를 순차 적용하고 파트너십을 확장할 방침이다. 이를 통해 광고주는 정밀한 타깃팅 기반의 ROI·ROAS 성과를 거두고, 언론사는 다양한 포맷의 맞춤 기사 유통과 타임라인을 통한 과거 기사 재소비 효과를 얻을 수 있다.

2026년 경기도 AI 멤버십 선정 및 서울시립대학교 인공지능학과와의 산학협력으로 AI 기술력을 고도화해온 허블은 향후 언론사별 콘텐츠 모듈화와 독립형 AI 에이전트 앱 출시를 단계적으로 추진한다.

허블은 11월 19일부터 21일까지 부산 벡스코에서 열리는 '지스타 2026' B2B 전시관에서 탭뷰 AI를 최초로 공개한다.

황고연 허블 대표는 “누구나 같은 길이의 기사를 읽을 필요는 없다”며 “짧은 요약에서 멈추든, 사건 전체를 분석하든 각자 필요한 수준의 정보를 얻는 경험이 탭뷰 AI의 핵심”이라고 말했다.

황수환 허블 본부장은 “허블뷰를 통해 구축한 100여 개 제휴 앱과 300만 명 규모의 이용자 기반이 탭뷰 AI의 사업 출발점”이라며 “기존 파트너 앱에 AI 뉴스 기능을 순차 도입하고 신규 제휴를 넓혀 500만 이용자 기반으로 확장하겠다”고 설명했다. 이어 “언론사별 콘텐츠 모듈화로 앱사와 언론사의 유통 협력을 강화하고, 독립형 AI 에이전트 앱까지 사업을 발전시킬 계획”이라고 덧붙였다.

정부가 비수도권 광역자치단체 10곳 가운데 6곳을 창업도시로 추가 선정한다. 선정된 창업도시는 2030년까지 4년간 600억원 안팎의 직접 지원 예산을 받는다.

중소벤처기업부는 이같은 내용의 '창업도시 조성 프로젝트' 추가 공모를 23일 시작한다고 밝혔다.

프로젝트는 지역의 인재, 기술, 자본을 한데 모아 창업기업의 지역 창업과 성장, 정착을 돕기 위해 올해 시작했다. 중기부는 올해 상반기 과학기술원이 있는 지역을 중심으로 대전, 대구, 광주, 울산 4곳을 선도모델로 선정했다.

이들 지방정부는 조성 전략을 세웠고 8월부터 사업화 자금과 창업교육, 실증, 개방형 혁신 지원을 받고 있다. 여기에 6곳이 더해지면 창업도시는 전국 10곳으로 늘어난다.

신청 대상은 5극 3특 가운데 수도권을 뺀 4극 3특 지역의 광역자치단체다. 충북, 충남, 세종, 경북, 부산, 경남, 전남, 강원, 전북, 제주가 해당한다.

신청하는 지방정부는 대표도시 1곳과 중심구역 1곳을 확보해야 한다. 지역이전 지원금 4억원과 엔젤투자허브 운영비 2억 4000만원을 합쳐 지방재원 6억 4000만원도 마련해야 한다. 운영기관인 창조경제혁신센터에는 전담인력 7명 이상을 둬야 하고, 창업도시 추진단도 최소 15개 이상 구성해야 한다.

선정된 창업도시에는 연간 150억원 규모 예산을 지원한다. 창업기업 지원금이 110억원, 운영기관 운영비가 40억원 안팎이다. 팁스(TIPS), 지역성장펀드, 엔젤투자허브 구축 등 정부 창업지원 사업도 연계한다.

접수는 23일부터 11월30일 오후 3시까지 받는다. 중기부는 연말부터 서류평가와 현장평가, 최종 심의를 진행해 2027년 1월 6곳을 최종 선정한다.

중국 우후 , 2026년 10월 22일 /PRNewswire/ -- 로드트립과 캠핑의 인기가 높아지며, 운전자들은 오프로드 차량에 험로 주파력을 넘어 편의성, 승차감, 실제 여행 상황 전반의 적응력까지 기대하게 됐다. 오프로드 기술이 실제 여행 수요를 어떻게 더 잘 충족할 것인가가 핵심 과제로 떠올랐다.

10월 21일, 2026 제투어 글로벌 테크놀로지 익스피리언스 데이의 오프로드 시승 행사가 저장성 모간산에서 열리며, 참가자들에게 산악 실전 체험의 기회를 제공했다. 전 세계 미디어와 KOL, 사용자 대표들은 T2와 G700 등 제투어 차량을 몰고 도강, 자갈길, 급경사, 크레이터 구간을 통과하며 전지형 주행 성능과 아웃도어 여행의 매력을 생생하게 체험했다.

Off-Road Treasure Hunt: JETOUR's Immersive Test-Drive Experience

제투어는 기존의 폐쇄형 테스트 트랙에서 벗어나, 15km 전지형 코스를 오프로드 트레저 헌트로 꾸몄다. 탐험 정신과 팀워크, 예상 밖의 짜릿함이 어우러진, 사용자 관점의 실전 오프로딩 시연이었다. 중남미 지역의 한 KOL은 "주행과 아웃도어 챌린지를 결합한 정말 흥미로운 시승 경험이었다"고 말했다.

별도로 마련된 캠프장에서는 실전 수요 기반의 체험 챌린지가 이어졌다. 유연한 수납 솔루션은 다양한 아웃도어 장비를 손쉽게 실을 수 있게 했고, 고출력 V2L 기능은 외부 전원 없이 현장에서 커피를 낼 수 있게 해 아웃도어에서도 일상의 편안함을 제공했다. 쓰러진 나무로 도로가 막힌 상황을 재현한 시연에서는 F700 의 견인 능력을 선보여, 구난과 트래블 트레일러 견인에서의 실용적 가치를 입증했다.

다양한 지형 테스트로 입증한 전지형 성능

도강 구간에서 운전자는 X 버튼 하나로 7+X 지능형 오프로드 시스템을 활성화해, 노면을 반복적으로 판단하거나 잠금 모드를 수동 전환할 필요가 없다. 비전 AI와 섀시 센서가 연동해 밀리초 단위로 주행 모드를 전환하고 토크를 배분한다.

캐멀험프와 크레이터 장애물 앞에서 G700의 GAIA 전지형 지능 플랫폼은 하이브리드 동력, 3개 디퍼렌셜 록, 에어 서스펜션, 지형 인식을 통합해 오프로드 성능과 승차감의 균형을 잡는다. 한 유럽 미디어는 "제투어는 극한 성능과 세련된 여행 경험의 균형을 잡아, 탐험 능력과 탑승객의 편안함을 모두 제공한다"고 평가했다.

스탈라이트 포럼 : 트래블 + 의 가치를 논하다

밤이 되자 스탈라이트 포럼에서 글로벌 게스트들이 하루의 경험을 나눴다. 커촨덩(Ke Chuandeng) 제투어 인터내셔널 총재와 옌쥔(Yan Jun) 수석 부총재가 트레저 헌트와 캠프 챌린지 우승팀에 시상하며 참여와 팀워크를 격려했다. 이어 게스트들은 시승과 캠핑 경험을 바탕으로 각 시장의 여행 수요와 여행의 미래에 대해 의견을 나눴다. 지형과 도로 조건, 여행 습관이 다륵면 오프로드 성능, 승차감, 일상적 편의성에 대한 요구도 달라진다는 데 공감하며, 기술이 다양한 여행 시나리오를 더 잘 지원하는 방안을 논의했다.

커촨덩 총재는 "제투어는 사용자의 실제 여행 수요에서 출발해 기술, 제품, 여행 라이프스타일을 통합한다"며 "트래블+ 전략 아래 아웃도어와 장거리 성능에 집중하면서 제품, 생태계, 문화 간의 연결을 깊게 해, 차량을 세계를 탐험하는 동반자로 만들고 있다"고 말했다.

앞으로도 제투어는 기술 혁신과 제품 개발을 통해 글로벌 사용자의 더 나은 여행에 대한 기대에 부응하며, 사람들이 자연과 조화롭게 탐험하고 여행할 수 있는 가능성을 넓혀 나갈 것이다.

2018년 출범한 제투어는 트래블+ 전략을 실천하며 전 세계 100여 개 국가 및 지역에 진출했고, 2,000여 개의 판매•애프터서비스 네트워크와 5,000만 명 이상의 글로벌 사용자를 보유하고 있다. 포트폴리오에는 라이트 오프로드 세그먼트의 T 시리즈와 프리미엄 럭셔리 오프로드 시장의 G 시리즈가 있으며, 도심 통근, 가족 로드트립, 아웃도어 캠핑, 장거리 여행 등 다양한 여행 시나리오를 아우른다.

Best Microsoft Surface Laptop (2026): Which Models to Buy and Avoid
items.summary: With pricing in flux and new models available, here’s which Surface Laptop and Surface Pro to buy.
items.content:
Microsoft’s Surface Line has a product to fit a variety of needs and budgets, including flexible 2-in-1 tablet-laptops. The company also recently announced new versions of its Surface Laptop and Surface Pro as follow-ups to its 2024 models, making it even trickier to pick the best model that matches your priorities.

When those 2024 Surface models launched, they were among my favorite devices of the year. Over the past couple of years, those models have held up, making them great buys—especially when on sale. But now, with the new Surface Laptop 8th Edition and Surface Pro 12th Edition (not to be confused with the Surface Pro 12), we finally have some next-gen silicon to pair with them. Just bear in mind that the new Snapdragon X2 chips come at much higher prices, bringing the devices’ value into question.

I weighed these details, among others, in outlining which Microsoft Surface device is best for every need.

Be sure to read our other buying guides for more, including the Best Laptops , Best Cheap Laptops , Best 2-in-1 Laptops , Best MacBooks , and our tips for choosing a laptop .

Updated October 2026: I've rewritten this guide with notes from my testing of the Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra and updated pricing for other models.

Recommending a laptop from 2024 as my top choice feels embarrassing. Not for me—but for Microsoft. I adore this laptop, and I actually still find myself returning to it over newer, flashier options. The 3:2 aspect ratio screen is my favorite feature, and it can't be found almost anywhere else right now. The taller shape of the display is preferred if you spend most of your time on a laptop looking at documents, spreadsheets, or websites. Beyond that, it gets great battery life, performs well (in just about anything other than games), and has a gorgeous, high-resolution display.

But I hear you say, why not the 2026 model (also known as the 8th Edition)? Microsoft launched a refresh this year with new chips inside (the Snapdragon X2 lineup, if you care to know). I've tested these chips in other laptops, such as the Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5x , and they speed things up in meaningful ways—especially on the graphics front. Unfortunately, Microsoft made the poor decision not to send these out to reviewers for independent testing, so I've never had one to try myself.

The real problem, though, is the pricing. Like many laptop manufacturers this year, Microsoft has dramatically increased the price of its products. You can thank the ongoing memory shortage for that. Right now, you can still buy the 2024 Surface Laptop with 512 GB of storage for $999 on Amazon. It's only for the Dune color right now, whereas the Black and Silver models are $50 more. These are not quite as cheap as they were in 2025, but it's a great deal. It's especially affordable compared with the 2026 version. It's over $400 more for an otherwise identical configuration, and sometimes it jumps to the retail price of $1,600. That's just too much for what you're getting. I just don't think the performance difference is worth that much. It'd be a different story if the 2024 model were unavailable, but I have a hard time suggesting someone buy the newer one at the moment.

The Surface Laptop comes in two main variants: 13.8-inch and 15-inch screen sizes. Both are great, but I think the 13.8-inch model offers plenty of screen real estate for the average person, especially with this aspect ratio.

The Surface Laptop Ultra might bear some resemblance to the standard Surface Laptop, but it's a completely different animal under the hood. It's no thicker than the 15-inch Surface Laptop, despite offering far more performance. That's thanks to the Nvidia RTX Spark N1X chip inside, which delivers GPU performance typically found only in discrete graphics cards, like those in gaming laptops. In many ways, this is Microsoft's answer to the MacBook Pro—a laptop designed for content creators, media pros, and a burgeoning new demographic: AI enthusiasts. It can be configured with up to 128 GB of unified RAM, allowing you to feed that GPU tons of memory to access larger AI models—all running entirely on-device. I tested the 32-GB version of the Surface Laptop Ultra, which limits you from running larger AI models (such as 70-billion parameters and above). In reality, you need something with a more powerful GPU to handle foundation-tier models that really compete with the cloud-based services people are used to. I don't know if the case for running local AI models is fully made yet, but the Surface Laptop Ultra lets you dip your toe in.

It can play games, too, but don't be fooled by the “Nvidia” brand into thinking it will perform anywhere near a proper discrete graphics card in a gaming laptop. Some very popular multiplayer games still aren't compatible at all (such as PUBG and League of Legends ), though Nvidia says it's working on it. The Surface Laptop Ultra is for someone who wants to dabble in content creation, gaming, and AI on their work laptop. And yes, if that sounds like the M5 Pro MacBook Pro, that's the point.

I’ve always liked the idea of a smaller Surface Pro, and in theory, the Surface Pro 12 (6/10, WIRED Recommends) checks the right boxes. It keeps the premium look and feel of the Surface Pro line, retaining the Snapdragon X Plus chip (with two fewer cores) while making slight changes to lower the price and make the tablet even thinner. I can live with the incremental downgrades in the webcam and display. My problem at launch, when I first reviewed the Surface Pro 12, was the pricing. Microsoft tried to slot this cheaper, smaller Surface below the Surface Pro 13.8, then immediately stopped selling the lower-tier configurations of that larger device to make room. But these days, the Surface Pro 13.8 has gotten so expensive that I no longer think it's worth buying. If you really want a 2-in-1 Windows tablet, the Surface Pro 12 is your best option.

items.title: Meta’s Ad Sales Are Suffering Now That Europeans Can Pick Less Personalization
items.summary: An earnings briefing on Wednesday revealed ad revenue has slowed since the European Union introduced the Less-Personalized Ads model at the beginning of this year.
items.content:
Advertising revenue in Europe continued to decelerate in the three months through September, the company said on Wednesday, underperforming its global figures. In the region, advertising revenue grew 18 percent year-on-year, slowing from the previous two quarters and lagging the 33 percent growth seen in the US and Canada.

Though Meta did not explicitly blame the introduction of the Less-Personalized Ads model on Wednesday, chief financial officer Susan Li had previously warned “we’re seeing the impact of less personalized ads offering in Europe now that it’s fully rolled out, and that may be an additional headwind,” in July’s second quarter results follow-up call. The preceding two quarters had seen advertising growth fall from around 40 percent to 24 percent; in the US and Canada, it had accelerated from 30 percent to 31 percent.

“We believe the EU’s free, personalized advertising option is contributing to the European slowdown,” Dominic Ball, equity research director at market analysis firm Rothschild & Co Redburn, told WIRED.

Meta began to offer Instagram and Facebook users the LPA option at the beginning of this year, after EU regulators ruled that it was breaching its Digital Markets Act obligation to give consumers the choice of an equivalent service that uses less of their personal data and hit the firm with a €200 million fine. Sales growth has slowed in the region since the start of the year, when Meta rolled out the option. The European Commission said that charging EU users who did not want their personal data used for personalized advertising for an ad-free service—a measure Meta introduced in the EU in November 2023—did not satisfy this. Meta does not disclose how many people have chosen each option.

LPA uses 90 percent less data than personalized ads, Meta says, with ads shown based on what a person sees in a particular session on the site, plus some data points like their age, location, and gender. It leads to poorer returns for EU advertisers, it warned in a response to the EU’s ruling. Less-personalized ads are less efficient, leading to fewer transactions, and more ads being closed due to being irrelevant or repetitive, it said. Indeed, the price advertisers were willing to pay per ad in Europe is not growing as fast as in the US and Canada, Wednesday’s results showed.

Li told investors on Wednesday the company has “a lot of runway” to increase ad conversions and efficiency, as it is “continuing to find ways to either enhance the actual performance of the recommendation engine.” Rothschild & Co Redburn’s Ball believes the company will be able to use AI to improve its ad targeting in Europe despite working with fewer personal data signals.

Investors were keen to understand how this fits into Meta’s personal AI agent, Muse , launched last month, questions about which dominated the call. Li said the company is seeing high commercial intent from people using Muse—asking for product recommendations, researching alternatives, and comparing options—which will allow them to eventually tap into the advertising market with that product.

여러 AI 모델 서비스를 하나의 방식으로 연결하는 오픈소스 도구 라이트LLM(LiteLLM)의 1.107.0 버전에 악성 코드가 포함돼 배포됐다. 소프트웨어 공급망 보안 업체 세이프뎁(SafeDep)이 현지 시각 10월 21일 분석 결과를 공개했다. 라이트LLM은 개발자가 오픈AI와 앤트로픽 등 여러 AI 서비스를 같은 방식으로 사용하도록 돕는 도구다.

테크크런치에 따르면 공격자는 파이썬 패키지 저장소 PyPI와 도커 허브, 깃허브 컨테이너 저장소에 변조된 파일을 업로드했다. 악성 코드는 파이썬이 실행될 때마다 작동해 SSH 키와 클라우드 접속 정보, 개발 자동화용 비밀 값, AI 서비스 인증 정보, 브라우저에 저장된 비밀번호를 수집한다. 수집한 정보는 암호화한 뒤 라이트LLM 공식 주소와 비슷한 가짜 주소로 전송한다.

함께 설치되는 백도어는 1시간마다 깃허브 파일에서 명령 서버 주소를 읽고, 정보 수집을 반복하며 외부 코드를 내려받아 실행한다. 백도어는 공격자가 시스템에 몰래 원격 접속할 수 있게 하는 악성 프로그램이다. 세이프뎁은 공식 소스 코드에 없는 설정 문구가 배포 파일에 추가된 점을 근거로, 배포 과정이 침해됐거나 PyPI 계정 정보가 도난당한 것으로 추정했다.

세이프뎁은 1.106.2 버전과 1.107.0 정식 출시 전 시험판 2종은 정상이라고 밝혔다. 설치 폴더에 cook.pth와 cook.py, sitecustomize.py 파일이 있으면 감염 흔적으로 볼 수 있다. 라이트LLM은 악성 버전과 컨테이너 이미지를 삭제하고 대응 안내를 공개했다. 테크크런치는 같은 날 PHP와 노드js에서도 심각한 보안 결함이 공개돼 기업 보안팀의 대응 부담이 증가했다고 전했다.

items.title: I Worked for a Whole Day Using Only the iPhone Duo. Here’s How It Went
items.summary: A portable keyboard and kickstand make it a viable emergency workstation—even if iOS still gets in the way.
items.content:
An iPhone 18 Pro is $1,199. An iPad is $449. If you want both—the iPhone as your primary device and the iPad to handle some work when you’re away from your desk—you'll be spending a total dollar amount that’s pretty close to the $1,999 price of Apple’s first folding smartphone , the iPhone Duo .

So can the Duo’s 7.6-inch screen pull double duty as a phone and a workstation? Does it make sense to shell out a few hundred more dollars for a single gadget that can theoretically handle the workload of two devices?

I wrote my entire iPhone Duo review on Apple’s new handset. I used a note-taking app called Bear , which was mercifully optimized for the Duo’s larger screen. ( Read my review and you’ll hear about how most apps aren’t optimized; it could take weeks or months for everything to look right.) But surprisingly, I didn’t hate the experience.

I have run this experiment before on Android foldables and even smart glasses with virtual workspaces , but iOS has its own unique hurdles. Notably, iOS doesn’t recognize a Bluetooth mouse or trackpad by default. Instead, you have to go to the phone’s accessibility settings and enable AssistiveTouch—then you’ll get an iPad-like cursor that lets you navigate the Duo’s interface and select text without constantly reaching for the touchscreen.

Even with the cursor, small tasks like pasting hyperlinks into a written piece or quickly Googling topics for additional research are slower and more cumbersome, so I left those for the end when I moved everything into WIRED’s content management system. Even then, I had to switch over to my desktop for the final touches.

Apple also imposes arbitrary multitasking restrictions in iOS because, well, Apple likes to control how people use its devices. For example, if you open two apps in split screen mode, you can only view them in an equal 50-50 split. Unlike most operating systems that let you adjust how much of each app you can see by dragging the border in between the windows, iOS leaves you stuck with a view that gives both apps equal screen space. If you want to use the iPhone in portrait orientation and stack two apps vertically, one on the top part of the screen and the other on the bottom, you’re out of luck. In portrait mode, you can only pin video apps to the top with another app below.

One thing Apple did get right is app pairs. You can “pin” two apps together, and they will live in your Recents, ready when you need them. Say you always want to look at your email and calendar together; you can pair them and find them in Recents whenever you need them. (Tap the bar in the middle to lock and save the pair.)

My keyboard of choice is an old Seenda folding Bluetooth keyboard that is admittedly not very good. I imagine we'll see an array of compact keyboards hitting the market soon—like Nillkin or ProtoArc keyboards already available now—to cater to workaholics who need to work everywhere . I also used one of Apple's cases, the iPhone Duo Folio with Kickstand , to keep the phone propped up. You can use various MagSafe kickstands , tripods , or cases with the Duo.

I typed most of the day, but I also had to juggle between apps to respond to coworkers or hop on a Zoom call. Thankfully, the Slack iOS app updated the day before my testing to fully support the iPhone Duo's larger screen and vertical navigation, making it very easy to bounce between multiple conversations in the two-pane view. I still think Apple should add a feature like the iPad's Slide Over , where you can “hide” a floating app off to the side and bring it back in when you need it. It’d be the perfect spot for messaging apps like Slack, WhatsApp, or Messages, and it wouldn’t interrupt your split screen experience.

Zoom wasn’t optimized for the Duo, though my editor said the video quality from the inner and outer selfie cameras was “really good.” I used the folio kickstand to Zoom on the big 7.6-inch screen until we realized my video was stuck in an awkward portrait orientation, so I laid the phone down on the table and pointed the 5.4-inch outer screen toward my face, which made it feel like a traditional laptop experience.

The app that annoyed me the most was Gmail. Even though Google updated the Google Search app to be compatible with the iPhone Duo early this week, the rest of Google's workspace apps currently look awful on the Duo. I imagine full support will come very soon, if not on Friday, when the Duo officially launches. The two-pane view in Gmail (or any email app) is a game changer for clearing a bunch of emails when you’re on the go.

By 6 pm, battery life was sitting around 45 percent, which is very impressive. That's with around six hours of screen-on time.

You probably won’t want to replace your laptop with the iPhone Duo. And anyone accustomed to the iPad’s larger screen may feel cramped on the Duo's 7.6-inch canvas. But with a kickstand and the right portable keyboard? Knocking out focused, light work on the Duo is entirely doable. Things will get even more interesting once Apple Pencil support arrives later this year.

But as I packed up my keyboard, I couldn’t shake a familiar feeling. Maybe we’ll realize a single do-it-all device isn’t as great as it’s chalked up to be. Maybe it is better to kick back with a dedicated MP3 player . Or snap photos with a camera . Or write in a notebook . Or work off a laptop.

Speaking of which, did you hear Apple’s making a touchscreen MacBook ?

유럽의 마지막 페니실린 공장이 문을 닫을 위기에 놓였다는 소식, 들어보셨나요? 오스트리아 쿤들 공장이 그 주인공인데요, 세계 원료약 시장의 약 80%를 중국이 차지하면서 값싼 중국산 원료에 밀려 유럽 대다수의 페니실린 공장이 이미 문을 닫았어요. 사실 이 위기는 2000년대 초 유럽 기업들이 비용을 아끼려고 생산 기지를 아시아로 옮기면서 시작됐는데요, 팬데믹과 전쟁이 터지고 나서야 약 공급이 끊길 수 있다는 걸 실감하게 됐어요.

우리나라도 남의 일이 아니에요. 싼 수입약을 많이 들이면 건강보험이 내는 약값이 줄어서 당장은 이득처럼 보이지만, 국내 공장의 가동률이 떨어지고 해외 의존이 깊어져요. 그러다 전쟁이나 무역분쟁 같은 위기가 오면 품절과 가격 폭등으로 건보 재정과 환자가 함께 타격을 입게 되죠.

그래서 자국 공장을 지키는 일은 위기 때 쓸 보험료를 미리 내는 것과 같다고 해요. 전면 수입 대체의 위험도는 10점 만점에 8점으로 평가될 만큼 가볍게 볼 문제가 아니에요.

다만 공짜 지원은 없어요. 조건을 지킨 공장만 지원금을 받고, 어기면 돌려받는 구조인데요. 목표를 이루면 2년을 연장하는 3+2년 계약, 석 달 치 약을 쌓아 두는 90일 비축, 원료를 3개국 이상에서 들여오는 조건을 걸어야 한데요. 계약을 3년으로 할지 5년으로 할지는 토론에서 가장 크게 부딪친 쟁점이었고요, 지원금을 건보와 국고 중 어디서 낼지는 아직 남은 숙제예요. 우리의 의료주권을 위한 더 자세한 내용은 AI의눈 보고서에서 확인해보세요!

진요한 상무, 서울 데브데이서 도입 경험 공유…직원 교육과 보안·비용 관리 병행

컴퓨팅 입력 :2026/10/22 19:20

LG CNS가 기업용 인공지능(AI) 서비스 '챗GPT 엔터프라이즈' 국내 이용자 약 3만 명을 확보했다고 밝혔다.

LG CNS는 22일 서울 강남구 라움 아트센터에서 열린 '오픈AI 데브데이 익스체인지: 서울'에서 챗GPT 엔터프라이즈 공급 현황을 공개했다. 올해 2월 시작한 오픈AI 리셀러 사업을 통해 금융과 유통, 바이오, 제조 등 고객사 임직원 약 3만 명이 챗GPT 엔터프라이즈 서비스를 사용하고 있다고 했다.

이날 발표에 나선 진요한 LG CNS AI센터장 상무는 기업 고객에게 제품 공급뿐 아니라 업무 적용과 직원 교육, 보안·비용 관리도 지원한다고 설명했다. 기업에서는 챗GPT를 사내 데이터와 업무 시스템에 연결하고 직원별 접근 권한과 사용 비용도 관리해야 하기 때문이다.

LG CNS는 고객사에서 챗GPT를 활용할 업무를 찾는 작업도 맡는다. 한 법무법인에서는 업무를 수십 개 영역으로 나눠 챗GPT를 어디에, 어느 정도까지 적용할 수 있는지 분석했다. 이후 법무법인과 함께 업무별 활용 사례를 만들며 조직 내 사용을 확대했다.

진 상무는 개인에게 익숙한 챗GPT라도 기업에 적용하려면 별도 준비가 필요하다고 강조했다. 개인용과 기업용 서비스 화면이 비슷해 도입이 쉬울 것이라는 기대가 생기지만 실제로는 기업마다 다른 시스템과 보안 환경을 고려해야 한다고 지적했다.

AI가 질문에 답하는 단계를 넘어 직접 업무를 처리하면서 관리 범위도 넓어졌다. 진 상무는 AI가 사내 데이터를 활용하는 과정에서 어떤 작업을 수행할 수 있고 어느 단계에서 통제를 받아야 하는지 파악해야 한다고 설명했다.

그는 "회사 용어만 알아도 되는 게 아니라 권한도 이해해야 하고 어디서 통제돼야 하는지도 이해해야 한다"고 강조했다.

진 상무는 사용 비용도 주요 과제로 꼽았다. AI가 처리하는 데이터 단위인 '토큰' 사용량이 급증하는 경우가 있어 이를 관리하면서 업무에 활용하도록 도와야 한다고 밝혔다. LG CNS는 서비스 도입 이후에도 고객사에 AI 사용량과 비용 관리를 지원하고 있다.

진 상무는 새 AI 모델이 등장하는 속도와 기업이 이를 실제 업무에 적용하는 속도에는 차이가 있다고 지적했다. 규제와 망 분리 등을 고려하면서 사내 지식과 업무 절차를 AI에 연결하는 데 시간이 필요하기 때문이다.

LG CNS는 기존 IT 시스템 구축 경험과 보안 기술을 바탕으로 기업 AI 전환(AX)을 지원한다. 자체 플랫폼 '에이전틱웍스'를 활용한 사업과 오픈AI 등 외부 AI 기업과 협력을 병행한다.

보안 분야에서는 오픈AI 협력 프로그램 '데이브레이크' 파트너 참여를 추진하고 있다. 데이브레이크는 기업이 AI로 제품과 서비스에서 보안 취약점을 찾고 검증한 뒤 수정·패치하도록 지원하는 프로그램이다. 진 상무는 LG 계열사와 금융 등 여러 산업에서 쌓은 보안 경험을 바탕으로 관련 서비스를 개발하고 있다고 밝혔다.

그는 "AX는 단순히 성능이 우수한 AI 모델을 도입하는 데 그치지 않고 데이터 정비와 거버넌스, 운영체계 수립 등을 종합적으로 고려하는 것"이라며 "기존 기업 시스템과 업무를 AI 기반으로 전환해야 진정한 AX를 실현할 수 있다"고 말했다.

items.content:
31일까지 홋카이도·규슈·오사카 등 여행상품 릴레이 방송

유통/생활/문화 입력 :2026/10/22 19:18

SK스토아가 하나투어와 손잡고 일본 여행상품을 집중 판매한다. 가을 단풍과 겨울 온천 여행 수요를 겨냥해 지역별 패키지를 선보이고, 인공지능(AI) 인플루언서를 활용한 방송 콘텐츠도 마련했다.

SK스토아는 오는 31일까지 'SK스토아X하나투어 트래블 페스타'를 진행한다고 22일 밝혔다.

이번 특집전은 일본 홋카이도와 규슈, 고베·오사카 등 주요 관광지를 중심으로 구성했다. 온천 리조트와 전통 료칸 숙박, 현지 특식 등을 결합한 패키지 상품을 순차적으로 판매한다.

먼저 23일 오후 10시 31분과 24일 오후 11시 21분에는 '홋카이도 3박 4일' 상품을 방송한다.

도야 썬팔래스 리조트 등 온천 호텔 2박과 삿포로 시내 호텔 1박으로 구성했다. 게 샤브샤브 등 6가지 특식과 삿포로 눈 축제, 화이트 일루미네이션 등 겨울 관광 일정도 포함했다. 가이드 경비와 선택 관광이 없는 상품이다.

규슈 여행상품은 2박 3일과 3박 4일 일정으로 선보인다. 힐튼 후쿠오카 시호크와 벳푸 스기노이 호텔, 츠에타테 온센 히젠야 등 숙박시설을 활용하고 일본 전통 코스요리인 가이세키 등을 포함했다.

30일과 31일에는 고베·오사카 여행상품을 판매한다. 비와코 그랜드 온천 료칸 숙박과 고베 야경 관광 등을 결합했다.

방송에서는 AI 기술을 활용한 여행지 소개 영상도 선보인다.

AI 인플루언서 '안나'가 교토 청수사와 도게츠교, 오사카 도톤보리 등 주요 관광지를 안내하는 방식이다. 스튜디오에도 AI 합성 기술을 적용해 현지 바다와 관광지 풍경을 배경으로 구현한다.

고객 참여 행사도 진행한다. 특집전 기간 매 방송에서 추첨을 통해 2명에게 각각 50만원 상당의 하나투어 여행상품권을 제공한다. 전체 경품 규모는 1천100만원이다.

SK스토아 모바일 앱에서는 '라이브톡'을 운영한다. 여행상품 담당 프로듀서(PD)와 상품기획자(MD)가 고객 질문에 실시간으로 답하고 여행 일정과 상품 정보를 안내한다.

신희권 SK스토아 커머스본부장은 "일본 여행 수요가 이어지는 가운데 가을 단풍부터 겨울 설경까지 즐길 수 있는 상품을 준비했다"며 "하나투어와 협력해 다양한 여행상품과 고객 혜택을 제공하겠다"고 말했다.
